title: Whiplash Injury Claims in New Orleans
metaDescription: Whiplash injury claims in New Orleans: medical documentation, insurer tactics, and 1-year LA deadline.
excerpt: Educational New Orleans, LA guide — 1-year SOL, local hospitals, and insurer tactics. Not legal advice.

sections.heading: First 10 minutes: safety and 911
paragraphs: A collision on I-95 or surface streets in New Orleans can escalate quickly. If vehicles are drivable and it is safe, move to a shoulder or parking lot. Turn on hazard lights.
Call 911 when anyone reports pain, airbags deploy, fluids leak, or traffic is blocked. New Orleans County dispatch will route New Orleans police or state patrol depending on location.
list: Stay inside the vehicle with seatbelts on if traffic passes closely at highway speed
Do not admit fault — describe facts only
Request a crash report number before officers leave

sections.heading: New Orleans documentation checklist
paragraphs: Photograph all vehicles, license plates, VIN stickers, skid marks, traffic signals, and visible injuries. New Orleans insurers expect timestamped photos.
Collect names and phone numbers from witnesses — independent accounts matter on I-95, I-75, US-1 and in New Orleans County.
Exchange insurance policy numbers and registration; note employer if the other driver was working.

sections.heading: Medical care within 24 hours
paragraphs: New Orleans has New Orleans Regional Medical Center and New Orleans General Hospital among its major facilities. Level I trauma care is available at New Orleans Level I Trauma Center.
Whiplash, concussion, and internal injuries may appear hours later. A same-day urgent care or ER visit creates a medical record insurers cannot easily dismiss.

sections.heading: Louisiana reporting rules
paragraphs: Louisiana requires crash reporting when injuries, death, or significant property damage occur. Minimum liability limits are 15/30/25.
Cooperate with officers; request a copy of the report through the investigating agency. If police do not respond, check https://www.dotd.la.gov/ for self-report thresholds.

sections.heading: Insurance notification without hurting your claim
paragraphs: Notify your carrier with basic facts — date, location, vehicles involved. Decline recorded statements until you understand your coverage and injuries.
Louisiana uses Pure comparative comparative negligence; anything you say can affect fault allocation.

sections.heading: Evidence preservation in New Orleans
paragraphs: Dashcam, Ring doorbell, and business security footage near New Orleans downtown interchange is often deleted within 7–30 days. Send written preservation letters when appropriate.
Save repair estimates, rental receipts, and mileage to medical appointments.

sections.heading: When to explore attorney matching
paragraphs: Consider a free consultation if you were hospitalized, fault is disputed, a commercial vehicle was involved, or the adjuster offers a quick settlement before treatment finishes.

faq.question: What is the statute of limitations in Louisiana?
faq.answer: Most injury claims face a 1-year deadline, but exceptions apply. Verify your dates with counsel.
